_comment: Frozen contract for whether a message asks a member for something, and why.
Everything that reacts to being asked must give the same answer: the herdr
doorbell (a wake queued with the reason), `await` (the message handed over
as the agent's turn), the wake digest (the message listed as asking for the
agent), an engine's summon and a persona's or worker's answer. The rule is
fastapi-backend/app/services/asks.py, the same for every sender and every
member, people, agents and engines alike:
Only what says something asks: an exchange with text. Presence,
keepalive, pings, notices and commits ask nobody.
Nobody asks themselves.
A mention asks: `mention`, or `interrupt` for @!.
Anything but a `reply` asks its recipients: `turn`.
A `reply` asks only whoever it mentions; its recipient is whoever the
replier last heard from, which `respond` fills in.
Nothing is stripped from what anyone writes. To name a member without
asking them, write @~name: a conductor summon written `@~a @~b` binds the
roles and wakes nobody but the conductor.
Each case is one message, written the way its sender writes it, and one
member. The cast: coder and planner are agents with herdr panes, hay is a
person posting from the app, aligner and conductor are engines of those
kinds, sage is a persona, builder is a worker, scribe is a synthesizer,
remote is an A2A agent. `sender` posts `text` in the room or the task's
thread (`where`). `to` is who an engine's turn or an A2A answer is for, or
who an agent last heard from before it replied. `shape` names a signal or
an engine turn when the sender alone doesn't say (`tick` is the aligner's,
through the turn primitive it calls). `asks` is the reason for `agent`, or
null.
fastapi-backend/tests/test_wake_paths_table.py writes each case through
the route or engine call that sends it and asserts asks() itself, the
doorbell, `await` and the digest all give `asks`.
